For statistical analysis, you can use Lee's L statistic for bivariate spatial correlation analysis, or another appropriate method of your choosing. You are testing whether GHG in one place relates to Crime in NEIGHBORING places.

Determine whether the two variables show a significant bivariate spatial relationship. Note: dedicated spatial-statistics packages (pysal, esda, libpysal, geopandas, or similar) are NOT installed in this environment -- don't spend turns trying different import paths for them. Implement this directly using only pandas and numpy. If you test statistical significance via a permutation/randomization test, use at least 500 random shuffles -- fewer permutations can produce an unstable p-value that lands on the wrong side of the 0.05 threshold just by chance, especially when the true effect is only moderate.

Every value you want to check or use as evidence must be wrapped in print(), e.g. print('Q1:', Q1). pandas and numpy are pre-imported as pd and np. import pandas as pd
```python
import numpy as np

DATASET_PATH = 'chunks_csv/bivariate/bivariate_2021_ghg_crime.csv'
ADJACENCY_PATH = 'chunks_csv/borough_adjacency.csv'

df = pd.read_csv(DATASET_PATH)
adj = pd.read_csv(ADJACENCY_PATH)

# Sort df by borough to have consistent ordering
df = df.sort_values('borough').reset_index(drop=True)
boroughs = df['borough'].tolist()
n = len(boroughs)
borough_to_idx = {b: i for i, b in enumerate(boroughs)}

# Build symmetric adjacency matrix
W = np.zeros((n, n))
for _, row in adj.iterrows():
    b1 = row['borough']
    b2 = row['neighbor']
    if b1 in borough_to_idx and b2 in borough_to_idx:
        i = borough_to_idx[b1]
        j = borough_to_idx[b2]
        W[i, j] = 1
        W[j, i] = 1  # ensure symmetry

# Check row sums
row_sums = W.sum(axis=1)
print('Row sums (min, max, mean):', row_sums.min(), row_sums.max(), row_sums.mean())
print('Boroughs with 0 neighbors:', [boroughs[i] for i in range(n) if row_sums[i] == 0])

# Row-standardize W
W_row = np.zeros_like(W)
for i in range(n):
    if row_sums[i] > 0:
        W_row[i, :] = W[i, :] / row_sums[i]
    else:
        W_row[i, :] = 0

S0 = W_row.sum()
print('S0:', S0)

# Get variables
x = df['GHG_value'].values
y = df['Crime_value'].values

# Mean-center
x_c = x - x.mean()
y_c = y - y.mean()

# Lee's L statistic
# L = (n / S0) * (x_c' W y_c) / sqrt((x_c' x_c)(y_c' y_c))
numerator = x_c @ (W_row @ y_c)
denominator = np.sqrt((x_c @ x_c) * (y_c @ y_c))
L_obs = (n / S0) * numerator / denominator

print('Lee L observed:', L_obs)

# Permutation test with 1000 shuffles
np.random.seed(42)
n_perm = 1000
L_perm = np.zeros(n_perm)

for i in range(n_perm):
    y_perm = np.random.permutation(y_c)
    num_perm = x_c @ (W_row @ y_perm)
    den_perm = np.sqrt((x_c @ x_c) * (y_perm @ y_perm))
    L_perm[i] = (n / S0) * num_perm / den_perm

# Two-tailed p-value
p_value = np.mean(np.abs(L_perm) >= np.abs(L_obs))
print('p-value:', p_value)
print('Mean of null:', L_perm.mean())
print('Std of null:', L_perm.std())
print('Min null:', L_perm.min())
print('Max null:', L_perm.max())
```

```python
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np

DATASET_PATH = 'chunks_csv/bivariate/bivariate_2021_ghg_crime.csv'
ADJACENCY_PATH = 'chunks_csv/borough_adjacency.csv'

df = pd.read_csv(DATASET_PATH)
adj = pd.read_csv(ADJACENCY_PATH)

# Drop NaN Crime row (City of London)
df = df.dropna(subset=['Crime_value']).reset_index(drop=True)
df = df.sort_values('borough').reset_index(drop=True)
boroughs = df['borough'].tolist()
n = len(boroughs)
borough_to_idx = {b: i for i, b in enumerate(boroughs)}

# Build symmetric adjacency matrix (binary)
W_binary = np.zeros((n, n))
for _, row in adj.iterrows():
    b1 = row['borough']
    b2 = row['neighbor']
    if b1 in borough_to_idx and b2 in borough_to_idx:
        i = borough_to_idx[b1]
        j = borough_to_idx[b2]
        W_binary[i, j] = 1
        W_binary[j, i] = 1

# Row-standardize W
row_sums = W_binary.sum(axis=1)
W_row = np.zeros_like(W_binary)
for i in range(n):
    if row_sums[i] > 0:
        W_row[i, :] = W_binary[i, :] / row_sums[i]

S0_binary = W_binary.sum()
S0_row = W_row.sum()
print('S0_binary:', S0_binary)
print('S0_row:', S0_row)

# Get variables
x = df['GHG_value'].values
y = df['Crime_value'].values
x_c = x - x.mean()
y_c = y - y.mean()

# Lee's L with row-standardized W
numerator_row = x_c @ (W_row @ y_c)
denominator = np.sqrt((x_c @ x_c) * (y_c @ y_c))
L_row = (n / S0_row) * numerator_row / denominator
print('Lee L (row-standardized):', L_row)

# Lee's L with binary W
numerator_bin = x_c @ (W_binary @ y_c)
L_bin = (n / S0_binary) * numerator_bin / denominator
print('Lee L (binary W):', L_bin)

# Permutation test with binary W, 5000 shuffles
np.random.seed(42)
n_perm = 5000
L_perm_bin = np.zeros(n_perm)

for i in range(n_perm):
    y_perm = np.random.permutation(y_c)
    num_perm = x_c @ (W_binary @ y_perm)
    den_perm = np.sqrt((x_c @ x_c) * (y_perm @ y_perm))
    L_perm_bin[i] = (n / S0_binary) * num_perm / den_perm

p_value_bin = np.mean(np.abs(L_perm_bin) >= np.abs(L_bin))
print('p-value binary (5000 perm):', p_value_bin)

# Permutation test with row-standardized W, 5000 shuffles
L_perm_row = np.zeros(n_perm)
for i in range(n_perm):
    y_perm = np.random.permutation(y_c)
    num_perm = x_c @ (W_row @ y_perm)
    den_perm = np.sqrt((x_c @ x_c) * (y_perm @ y_perm))
    L_perm_row[i] = (n / S0_row) * num_perm / den_perm

p_value_row = np.mean(np.abs(L_perm_row) >= np.abs(L_row))
print('p-value row-std (5000 perm):', p_value_row)
```
